segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: For decades, archaeologists believed that complex societies and the monumental architecture, the large buildings signifying them, only emerged after agriculture, and that farming was essential for societal development.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: After all, before agriculture developed, people tended not to settle in a single place, but moved from place to place in search of food.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: We call such people nomadic hunter-gatherers.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: They were continuously on the move to hunt and collect food.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: And for people who aren't settled, it was more practical to live in small mobile groups rather than in complex societies.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: But the excavation of the ancient site of Göbekli Tepe threw a wrench in this whole story.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: Göbekli Tepe, dating back about 11,000 years, consists of multiple massive pillars arranged in circles and is considered the world's oldest known temple.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: Remarkably, it predates the earliest evidence of agriculture in the area by several thousand years.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: This suggests spiritual practices, not agriculture, may have caused early communities to form.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: Many scholars interpret the site as a ceremonial center, a periodic gathering place for nomadic hunter-gatherers.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: More recently, archaeologists there did find traces of things like food-processing areas, stone tools for grinding grains, as well as actual plant residues.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: Yet these residues come from local wild grains, not domesticated crops, and the structures may not indicate year-round habitation.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: So while Göbekli Tepe might have hosted temporary gatherings, the evidence still supports the idea that spiritual practices played a central role in early societal development.
